name: Sufjan Stevens
label: Asthmatic Kitty
lede: A banjo, a plan to write an album for every state, and 25 years later he's still on the label he started with his stepfather, with Javelin the sixth-best record of 2023 according to Pitchfork.

eras.title: A kid from Alanson, a cat with asthma
eras.text: Born in Detroit, raised in northern Michigan, Sufjan Stevens learns oboe and banjo, goes to Hope College and starts a record label with his stepfather. The label is named after a cat.

years.h: Sufjan Stevens is born in Detroit
years.p: He moves to Alanson, Michigan, at age nine, then goes through Interlochen Arts Academy and Hope College in Holland.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists a school run that includes Detroit Waldorf School, Alanson Public Schools, Interlochen Arts Academy and Harbor Light Christian School. He graduated from Hope College Phi Beta Kappa, and later earned an MFA in creative writing from The New School in New York.

years.h: Hope College: a folk band, a garage band, a stint with Danielson
years.p: At Hope he joins the folk-rock band Marzuki and the garage outfit Con Los Dudes, and plays with the Danielson Famile.
years.xp: The Danielson Famile connection is one Stevens keeps for years. In his last semester at Hope he records what becomes his first solo album.

years.cap: Sufjan Stevens in 2015 on the Carrie and Lowell tour. · Wikimedia
years.src: Wikipedia: Asthmatic Kitty · Wikipedia: Sufjan Stevens
years.h: He and stepfather Lowell Brams start Asthmatic Kitty
years.p: The label is named for Sara, a stray cat with feline asthma that Brams adopted in 1994.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says Asthmatic Kitty was founded in 1999 by a community of musicians from Holland, Michigan, led by Stevens and [[Lowell Brams|4133fffc-c180-464e-b901-221b9c7e8c06]]. Sara's symptoms eased after Brams moved to Lander, Wyoming in 2002, thanks to the altitude and dry air. She died in December 2008, around fifteen or sixteen years old.

The label is now based in Bloomington, Indiana, and would release nearly everything Stevens makes for the next quarter century.

years.h: A Sun Came is out, and he plays fourteen instruments on it
years.p: Mostly recorded in Holland in 1998 on a four-track, with banjo, sitar, oboe and xylophone in the mix.
years.xp: Stevens described the sound himself as a mix of traditional pop, medieval instrumentation with Middle Eastern inflections, tape loops, digital samples, manic percussion and Arabic chants. Marzuki Stevens plays guitar, percussion and saxophone, and Shannon Stephens sings on a few tracks.

eras.title: Banjo, oboe and a fifty-state pledge
eras.text: Two records in, Stevens announces he'll write an album for every US state. The banjo and the state pride win him an audience, and the plan turns out to be more brand than blueprint.

years.h: Enjoy Your Rabbit: a Chinese zodiac record, in electronics
years.p: The follow-up to A Sun Came is a song cycle built on the animals of the Chinese zodiac, and a long way from the banjo records that followed.
years.xp: It is the record that tells you the banjo was never the whole plan. He would come back to synths and drum machines on The Age of Adz nine years later.

years.h: Michigan: a love letter to the state he grew up in
years.p: Recorded with two Shure SM57s and an AKG C1000 in spots like Petoskey and Brooklyn. Pitchfork gave it 8.5.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's Brandon Stosuy called it a beautiful, sprawling homage, and noted some tracks ran long. By 2005 it had sold 27,000 copies in the US, according to Wikipedia. The cover is hand-painted by Laura Normandin, a crafts editor at Martha Stewart Living.

Its song "Redford" would later inspire the title and structure of The Roots' 2011 album.

q: Sufjan Stevens, as summarized by Wikipedia
years.h: The 'Fifty States' plan gets announced, then quietly shelved
years.p: After Michigan he says he'll do all fifty states. Illinois is the only other one he makes.
years.xp: Stevens later acknowledged the fifty states pitch was a promotional gimmick that he never seriously planned to finish, according to Wikipedia. The stunt still worked: it gave a banjo-and-oboe folk musician a story journalists could not resist.

years.h: Seven Swans: banjo, Abraham and the Transfiguration
years.p: Recorded at Daniel Smith's home studio and the New Jerusalem Rec Room in Clarksboro, NJ. Pitchfork gave it 8.1.
years.xp: The Guardian called it a record of remarkable delicacy, and Spin described it as Elliott Smith after ten years of Sunday school. It came out on Sounds Familyre, and Asthmatic Kitty reissued it in 2016.

eras.title: Illinois, and the Illinoisemakers
eras.text: The breakthrough arrives with 22 tracks and song titles that read like footnotes. Stevens builds a touring orchestra, dumps a heap of outtakes, and makes five discs of Christmas music.

years.h: Illinois: 22 tracks with titles the length of a paragraph
years.p: Recorded in Queens and around New York. Pitchfork gave it 9.2 and later placed it No. 16 on its 2000s list.
years.xp:
Metacritic scores it 90/100. It is Stevens's first Billboard 200 entry, peaking at No. 121, and the RIAA certified it Gold in 2017, per Wikipedia. It also includes "John Wayne Gacy, Jr.", a song about the Chicago serial killer.

The original cover shows Superman; DC Comics required its removal from later pressings. His live band, the Illinoisemakers, is a group of eight to ten string players and singers.

years.h: "Chicago" becomes his most-licensed song
years.p: It ends up in Little Miss Sunshine, Veronica Mars, The Politician and, as a demo, The Bear.
years.xp: Stevens cut five versions, including an acoustic take and an arrangement he labeled Adult Contemporary Easy Listening. The RIAA has certified it Gold, and Pitchfork put it in The Pitchfork 500.

years.h: Songs for Christmas: five discs of original carols and standards
years.p: Recorded annually from 2001 (skipping 2004), it began as an exercise in learning to appreciate the holiday.
years.xp: He'd follow it with Silver & Gold in 2012, 58 more songs, bringing the total to 100 Christmas tracks. That year's tour was titled the "Sirfjam Stephanapolous Christmas Sing-a-Long Seasonal Affective Disorder Spectacular Music Pageant Variety Show Disaster."

years.cap: Sufjan Stevens performing at Chicago's Metro, 2012-12-15 · Wikimedia
years.h: The BQE sells out the 2,109-seat BAM Opera House
years.p: A 30-minute symphonic tribute to Brooklyn's expressway, with 36 performers, hula hoopers and a Super 8 film he shot himself.
years.xp: Wikipedia says it sold out with no advertising. It later won the 2008 Brendan Gill Prize.

eras.title: Synths, a virus and a lot of side projects
eras.text: Stevens blows up his own sound with a 25-minute electronic epic, tours it in costume, and spends four years on collaborations. Then his mother dies.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Age of Adz · Wikipedia: Sufjan Stevens
years.h: The Age of Adz swaps banjo for glitch and hip-hop beats
years.p: Inspired by the outsider artist Royal Robertson, it opens up with a 25-minute closer, "Impossible Soul". Pitchfork gave it 8.4.
years.xp:
Stevens said a mysterious, debilitating virus that affected his nervous system in 2009 and 2010 shaped the record, and that he was getting more in touch with his physical self. It debuted at No. 7 on the Billboard 200 with 36,000 copies, his best opening at that time, per Wikipedia.

The All Delighted People EP had arrived on August 20, and reached No. 27 on the Billboard 200 on digital sales alone.

years.h: S/S/S: Beak & Claw with Son Lux and Serengeti
years.p: A three-way EP on Anticon, and the first of two rounds with the trio.

years.h: His mother, Carrie, dies of stomach cancer
years.p: She had left the family when he was an infant. The album it eventually leads to is Carrie & Lowell.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports that Carrie struggled with depression, schizophrenia and substance abuse. In the years that followed Stevens turned the loss into the songs on his 2015 record.

eras.title: Carrie, Lowell and a red carpet
eras.text: The quietest record he'd made becomes the one everybody talks about. Two years later a movie soundtrack takes him to the Oscars.

years.src: Wikipedia: Carrie & Lowell · Stereogum: Carrie & Lowell Turns 10
years.h: Carrie & Lowell: the grief record, named for his mother and stepfather
years.p: Recorded across Brooklyn, Portland, Oklahoma, Wisconsin and a Klamath Falls hotel room on an iPhone. Pitchfork gave it 9.3.
years.xp:
Producer Thomas Bartlett (Doveman) shaped the sparse sound. Stevens told the press: "I was recording songs as a means of grieving, making sense of it. But the writing and recording wasn't the salve I expected." It debuted at No. 10 on the Billboard 200.

Pitchfork ranked it No. 6 for 2015, and raised its own score to 10 for the 10th anniversary, according to Wikipedia. Stereogum put it 16th on its decade list.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mystery of Love · The Fader: Watch Sufjan Stevens perform Mystery Of Love at the Oscars
years.h: He plays "Mystery of Love" at the Oscars in a pink Gucci tux
years.p: Chris Thile, Moses Sumney and St. Vincent back him. The song lost to "Remember Me" from Coco.
years.xp:
Director Luca Guadagnino first asked Stevens to narrate Call Me by Your Name. Stevens declined and offered original music instead, with full creative control. The soundtrack came out on December 1, 2017, with "Mystery of Love", "Visions of Gideon" and a piano version of "Futile Devices".

He also earned a Grammy nomination, won Italy's David di Donatello for the song in 2019, and the song has gone platinum in the US, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Planetarium arrives as an 80-minute record with Dessner, Muhly and James McAlister
years.p: The five-year-old live project finally gets a studio album.

eras.title: Ambient, and a lot of it
eras.text: He goes deep into synthesizers, meditation and a concept album made with a friend, on his own label as ever.

years.h: Aporia: 21 ambient tracks with Lowell Brams
years.p: A new age and ambient album made with the label co-founder.

years.h: The Ascension: 80 minutes, a 12-minute "America", a 7.0 from Pitchfork
years.p: He plays, records, arranges and mixes everything himself, with Casey Foubert and Bryce Dessner on guitar.
years.xp: Pitchfork's Sam Sodomsky called it kind of a drag. The New York Times put it No. 1 on its best albums of 2020 list, per Wikipedia, and Exclaim! gave it 10/10.

years.h: A Beginner's Mind with Angelo De Augustine
years.p: A concept album drawn from films of the 20th and 21st centuries.

eras.title: Javelin
eras.text: A death, an illness and a comeback album. Stevens returns to the quiet, singer-songwriter mode of Carrie & Lowell.

years.h: His partner Evans Richardson dies
years.p: Stevens publicly dedicated Javelin to him, according to Wikipedia.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes the dedication as the first time Stevens had publicly discussed Richardson or his own sexuality. Richardson worked as chief of staff at the Studio Museum in Harlem and had been elected chair of the American Alliance of Museums accreditation commission in 2021.

years.h: "So You Are Tired" is the first Javelin single
years.p: A shift back to scaled-down acoustic instrumentation, released with the announcement of the album.

years.h: Stevens says he has Guillain-Barré syndrome
years.p: He tells fans he is working through rehabilitation, including relearning to walk.

years.src: Wikipedia: Javelin (album) · Album of the Year: Sufjan Stevens - Javelin
years.h: Javelin: his first songs-first album since Carrie & Lowell
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.6, Best New Music, and ranked it No. 6 of 2023.
years.xp:
He recorded most of it alone at home, with Hannah Cohen, Megan Lui, Nedelle Torrisi, Adrienne Maree Brown and Pauline Delassus singing, and Bryce Dessner on guitar. It includes a Neil Young cover, "There's a World", and a track with baroque recorders, "My Red Little Fox".

Metacritic lists it at 87/100, and Album of the Year's critics average is 88. It peaked at No. 30 on the Billboard 200 and No. 7 in the UK.

eras.title: Illinoise goes to Broadway
eras.text: Twenty years on, the album that made his name becomes a dance musical.

years.cap: Sufjan Stevens, performing at the Celebrate Brooklyn festival · Wikimedia
years.src: Wikipedia: Sufjan Stevens · Wikipedia: Illinois (Sufjan Stevens album)
years.h: Illinoise opens in Chicago, then goes to Broadway
years.p: Justin Peck directs and choreographs a dance show built on Stevens's Illinois. It runs at the St. James Theatre April 24 to August 10.
years.xp: Story credit goes to Peck and Jackie Sibblies Drury, with Timo Andres handling orchestrations. It earned four Tony nominations, including Best Musical, and won Best Choreography for Peck.
